He has had a productive cough and recurrent chest infections all his life, together with chronic abdominal pain, diarrhoea and difficulty gaining weight. He also has diabetes mellitus. His chest X-ray suggests bronchiectasis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Bronchiectasis with pancreatic insufficiency, diabetes and male infertility (absent vas) is cystic fibrosis; sweat test and genotyping.

stem: A previously well 40-year-old man presents with a 3-day history of fever and shaking chills, including a 15-minute rigor. He also has a non-productive cough, anorexia and right-sided pleuritic chest pain, and has been breathless for 12 hours. Chest X-ray shows right middle lobe consolidation, and the full blood count shows neutrophilia with many band forms. Which of the following statements about this patient's pneumonia is correct?
option_A: If the sputum Gram stain shows many squamous epithelial cells and culture grows mixed flora, the patient probably has a viral infection
option_B: If the Gram stain shows numerous Gram-positive diplococci, numerous white cells and few epithelial cells, Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most likely pathogen
option_C: Although S. pneumoniae is the most likely cause, the diagnosis would be unlikely if blood cultures are negative
option_D: The absence of rigors would rule out pneumococcal pneumonia
option_E: A negative urinary pneumococcal antigen test excludes pneumococcal pneumonia
answer_text: If the Gram stain shows numerous Gram-positive diplococci, numerous white cells and few epithelial cells, Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most likely pathogen
explanation: A good sputum sample with Gram-positive diplococci and many neutrophils strongly supports S. pneumoniae.

stem: An obese 50-year-old woman complains of insomnia, daytime sleepiness, and fatigue. During a sleep study she is found to have recurrent episodes of arterial desaturationabout 30 events per hourwith evidence of obstructive apnea. Which of the following is the treatment of choice for this patient?

A 60-year-old obese male complains of excessive daytime sleepiness. He has been in good health except for mild hypertension. He drinks alcohol in moderation. The patient’s wife states that he snores at night and awakens frequently. Examination of the oropharynx is normal. Which of the following studies is most appropriate?
option_D: Study of muscles of respiration during sleep

stem: A 60-year-old man becomes short of breath 2 days after cholecystectomy. He has no fever, chills, sputum or pleuritic chest pain. Temperature 37.2 °C, pulse 75/min, respiratory rate 20/min, BP 120/70 mmHg. There are diminished breath sounds and dullness at the left base, and the trachea is shifted to the left. Chest X-ray shows a retrocardiac opacity obscuring the left hemidiaphragm. What is the most likely underlying problem?
option_C: Loss of volume of the left lower lobe (postoperative atelectasis)
answer_text: Loss of volume of the left lower lobe (postoperative atelectasis)
explanation: Tracheal shift towards a retrocardiac opacity after upper abdominal surgery is left lower lobe collapse (atelectasis); physiotherapy.

stem: A 55-year-old woman with long-standing chronic lung disease and recurrent episodes of acute bronchitis reports that her sputum, now produced daily and thick, has increased markedly over several months. There are flecks of blood in the sputum and she has lost 3.6 kg (8 lb). She has no fever or chills, and sputum cultures have not grown specific pathogens. Her chest X-ray and CT are shown. What is the most likely cause of her symptoms?
explanation: Dilated thick-walled bronchi larger than their arteries (signet ring) with daily sputum is bronchiectasis; investigate the cause.

stem: A 20-year-old firefighter attends the emergency department with headache and dizziness after helping to put out a garage fire. He is not breathless, and arterial blood gas shows a normal PaO2. What is the best first step in management?
option_A: Give high-flow 100% oxygen via a non-rebreather mask
option_C: Reassure him, as a normal PaO2 excludes significant poisoning
option_D: Obtain a CT scan of the head
answer_text: Give high-flow 100% oxygen via a non-rebreather mask
explanation: CO poisoning after smoke exposure (normal PaO2): give 100% oxygen via non-rebreather immediately; measure COHb by co-oximetry.

stem: An 18-year-old man's family have noticed blue discoloration of his nose, ears and fingers over the past few weeks. Which of the following statements is true?
option_B: Total haemoglobin is important in determining whether a patient will have cyanosis
option_C: Central cyanosis with hypoxia suggests methaemoglobinaemia or sulfhaemoglobinaemia
option_D: The presence of clubbing in a cyanotic patient confirms an acute cause of the cyanosis
option_E: Large amounts of methaemoglobin are required to produce cyanosis
answer_text: Total haemoglobin is important in determining whether a patient will have cyanosis
explanation: Cyanosis depends on total Hb (needs ~40–50 g/L deoxy-Hb): easy in polycythaemia, absent in severe anaemia.

explanation: Haemoptysis, anaemia and a fixed localised wheeze with gynaecomastia (ectopic hCG) is bronchial carcinoma.

explanation: Sudden pink frothy sputum, bilateral crackles, cold peripheries and hypotension is cardiogenic pulmonary oedema with shock.

explanation: Fever, rusty sputum and pleuritic pain with dullness and bronchial breathing is lobar pneumonia (pneumococcal).

stem: A 33-year-old farmer has recurrent dry cough and breathlessness several hours after starting work; he is febrile with diffuse end-inspiratory crackles, and the chest X-ray shows mid-zone mottling.
explanation: Fever, cough and breathlessness 4–8 h after work in a farmer is acute extrinsic allergic alveolitis (farmer's lung).

stem: An 18-year-old student has had fever, night sweats and cough for 3 months and increasing breathlessness for 2 weeks; there is reduced expansion with stony dullness and absent breath sounds over the right middle and lower zones.
